title: Analysing an unseen poem
keyIdea: On a first-read poem under time pressure: sum the gist, name speaker and situation, pin tone with evidence, then link two language/form/sound choices to effects that support one clear overall interpretation.
familyTip: Read a short unfamiliar poem once, ask for a one-sentence gist, then ask how one image shapes the mood — before naming any technique.

visual.caption: Strong unseen move or weak habit? Drag each, or tap it then a box.

items: sum gist in one or two sentences
treat speaker as always the poet
invent a plot the lines omit

lab.caption: Flagship lab: gist a short unseen poem, mark speaker/situation, pick tone, link method to mood, catch feature-spotting, order the response, then challenge.

kid: An unseen poem is one you have not studied. Start with a short gist: what happens or what is the situation?
Name the speaker (the voice in the poem, not always the poet) and the situation. Then choose a tone word that fits the evidence, such as lonely or bitter.
Pick concrete methods — an image, a sound pattern, a line break — and say how each one shapes mood or meaning. A technique name with no effect is weak.
Finish with a short overall reading that ties those methods together. Do not invent a plot the lines do not support.
adult: Ages 14 to 16. First-read poetry response: gist, speaker/situation, tone, methods with effects, overall interpretation. Distinct from forms-and-performance for younger learners.
Words: gist, speaker, situation, tone, imagery, form, sound, interpretation. Common mistakes: feature-spotting with no effect; speaker = poet always; inventing plot; device lists before gist.
In the lab the learner builds gist, speaker, tone and a method-to-mood link, then spots weak habits and orders a timed response.

practice.prompt: Best first move on an unseen poem?
choices: sum what happens in one or two sentences
ignore the last line on purpose
practice.hint: Get the situation clear before you hunt for techniques.
practice.explain: A clear gist anchors tone and method comments. Device lists first waste time.

choices: the voice in the poem (not always the poet)
practice.hint: Ask who seems to be talking in the lines themselves.
practice.explain: Speaker is the poem’s voice. It may be a persona, not the writer.

practice.prompt: In a {a}-minute unseen task you spend {b} minutes on gist and speaker. Minutes left for methods and writing?
practice.hint: Subtract planning minutes from the total time allowed for the task.
practice.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b} minutes remain for methods and the written response.

practice.prompt: You explain {a} images and {b} sound/form choices, each with an effect. How many method-with-effect points is that?
practice.hint: Add the image points to the sound or form points for a total count.

choices: list techniques with no link to meaning
practice.hint: Spot the weak exam habit that skips meaning.
practice.explain: Feature-spotting without effect does not build an interpretation.

choices: matched to evidence in word choice and pacing
a random mood word with no proof
pool.explain: Tone claims need textual evidence, not a guessed label.

pool.prompt: Open a timed unseen response with…
choices: a random list of poetic devices
rewriting the poem as prose only
pool.hint: Situation first. Use evidence from the lines to back the claim.
pool.explain: Gist first keeps later method comments anchored.

pool.prompt: You plan {a} minutes for gist+speaker and {b} for methods. Total planning minutes?
pool.hint: Add the gist-and-speaker block to the methods block for total planning time.

choices: tie methods to a clear reading of the poem
pool.explain: End by saying what the methods add up to — without inventing plot.

pool.prompt: Treating speaker as always the poet is…
choices: the same as naming the printer
pool.hint: Persona vs writer. Use evidence from the lines to back the claim.
pool.explain: Speaker and poet can differ; assume identity only with evidence.

pool.prompt: This lesson vs poetry performance forms is mainly about…
pool.explain: Here the skill is timed interpretation of an unfamiliar poem.

pool.prompt: You pick {a} images and write one clear effect for each. How many effects to write?
pool.hint: One clear effect per chosen image keeps the count honest.
pool.explain: Write {a} effects — one for each chosen image.

pool.prompt: Sound or form can matter when…
choices: you can say how they shape mood or meaning
pool.hint: Effect still required. Use evidence from the lines to back the claim.
pool.explain: Sound and form count when linked to meaning, not as bare labels.

pool.prompt: Inventing a plot the lines omit…
pool.hint: Stay with what the poem gives.
pool.explain: Build from the text. Invented plot drifts from evidence.
